steps.text: Wrap shrimp with 1/2 slice of bacon, securing with a toothpick. Be sure and use the large shrimp--the cooking time for the shrimp and the bacon is similar. If you use medium-sized shrimp, you might want to precook the bacon a little--over cooked shrimp are tough and rubbery--and a real shame.
Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).

Line a jelly roll pan with extra heavy duty foil, and place baking rack in the pan. Place the shrimp on the rack, and sprinkle heavily with the barbecue seasoning. Turn and sprinkle second side. Set aside for 15 minutes. The bacon will turn from creamy white to a little opaque, and the seasonings will soak in.

Bake in the preheated oven until bacon is crisp and shrimp are tender, 10 to 15 minutes. The rack keeps the shrimp from sitting in the draining bacon fat. With a little luck, you won't tear the foil--you can throw that away and only have to scrub the rack.

review.reviewBody: I've prepared a similar appetizer that involved making a small cut down the back of a large or jumbo peeled shrimp and inserting a slice of mild jalapeno pepper before wrapping with bacon. I've found that by winding 1/3 of a bacon slice, starting at one end and finishing at the other end to achieve a single thickness, the bacon has a better chance of cooking adequately and evenly. To cook, I heat the oven temp on the broil setting, add the wrapped shrimp, cook for 2 minutes, turn the shrimp over and broil for another 2 minutes, then turn the oven off and allow the shrimp to finish cooking as the temp gradually decreases. By the time the shrimp begins to turn pink, the bacon will be cooked.

I don't know if it was the bacon, or "Johnny's Grub Rub," also from this site, or both, but this was just spectacular. We partially cooked the bacon in the microwave to make sure it was cooked through without overcooking the shrimp. We also found that since the shrimp we used were the 21-25 count that they needed to be in the oven just nine minutes, so watch the cooking time carefully. I served this with Green Rice III and it was a match made in heaven. Words are inadequate to describe how delicious and beautiful this was.

I did not follow the recipe to the letter... For the barbecuing seasoning I used Penzey's 3000 barbecue spice blend. I put about 1 T on top of 13 (20-25) shrimp. I cut the butterfly deeper and stuck a sliver of jalapeno and then added a sliver of pepper jack cheese and wrapped with bacon. I only had thick bacon, so I nuked that for about 2.5 minutes to get it soft and pliable and used only 1/2 a piece of bacon for each shrimp. I then closed up my package with a toothpick. I broiled the shrimp for about 8 minutes. Armando, my other half, stated that this was a 9.5 out of 10 meal!! We served this with vegetable rice, tossed salad and some warm bread! Yummy!!!

I made this for a Superbowl party and everyone LOVED them I'm only giving 4 stars since I did change the recipe though. Here is my method... I used frozen shrimp (peel on), pre-cooked bacon (the kind in the box) and Masters Hand Fire & Brimstone Hot BBQ sauce and also their dry seasoning. I defrosted shrimp under cold running water, peeled them and then patted dry with paper towels. Seasoned both sides with BBQ dry seasoning. Wrapped each shrimp with 1/2 slice of bacon, securing with a toothpick. Then dunked/dredged each one in the BBQ sauce and placed on a broiler pan. I baked them at 450 for 10 min then dumped them in a pre-heated serving bowl. Everyone raved about them! Using the pre-cooked bacon eliminates the chance of the bacon being under-cooked and the shrimp being drowned in grease. It's also much faster than having to pre-cook raw bacon before wrapping the shrimp.

This was excellent! I had a request for shrimp tonight and this turned out to be a pleasant surprise! A big Mahalo to Naples34102 for mentioning the barbeque seasoning which she used for this shrimp recipe. I used a 26/30 count shrimp, that I cleaned, deveined and cut down the middle of the back. I partially cooked the bacon, then cut each slice into 1/3's using toothpick's to secure the bacon to the shrimp. I sprinkled just a little of, "Johnny's Grub Rub," from this website, onto the bacon and set it aside a while. I placed the shrimp onto a baking sheet that I sprayed with Pam. After the first 2 minutes, I turned the shrimp over to the other side to bake, then waited another 2-3 minutes until I saw the shrimp had turned the pink/orange color indicating it was cooked. I took them out from the oven since I did not want the shrimp to turn tough and rubbery. This was so delicious and flavorful. The shrimp is seasoned just right and the shrimp is cooked perfectly. What more could I ask from this dish?! Not difficult to prepare with nice results. It was a real hit with everyone and it was the very first thing that disappeared on everyone's plate! This was a real nice change from the normal shrimp dishes that we eat in this house. I served this dish with "Green Rice III," and "Carrots in Dill Butter," all from this website. Mahalo!

Recipe was so simple and so awesome! I used reviewer recommendation to place a thinly sliced strip of jalapeño ion the back of the shrimp before I wrapped it in bacon. I also used KC Masterpiece BBQ Seasoning (found in the spice aisle). Lastly. I followed recommendation to use 16 per pound count shrimp and used a full strip of center cut bacon. Will definitely make again!

It was fantastic, like others have said much better than a restaurant. I used thick cut bacon so I put it on the tray and popped it in the oven for about 7 minutes, let it cool then wrapped the shrimp. Next time I will put a paper towel down to catch the bbq rub (I used Killer Hogs bbq rub) then throw the paper towel away, the rub burned on the tin foil.
YUM Precooked thick cut applewood smoked bacon and used an applewood smoked rub. 6 min on one side 8 on the other and perfect for 12 ct very large shrimps.

I served these as an appetizer and they were quite good! I used high quality apple smoked bacon precooked a bit in the microwave. A baking sheet lined with foil was all I needed since precooking the bacon made a rack unnecessary since there was little grease. About eight minutes was all my 21-25 count shrimp needed in the oven. Seasoning and wrapping the shrimp the night before I served them worked perfectly.

Fantastique! I bought two pounds of shrimp, and I cut my [one pounds' worth of] bacon slices into thirds instead of halves. Had a little shrimp leftover (made a quick scampi out of them & threw in the fridge for later). I did not use toothpicks, the bacon ends overlapped perfectly so I put that side down on the rack. Used my broiling pan, worked perfectly. I was looking for a slam-dunk appetizer, this was definitely a hit!!
Delicious!!!...used Big E's BBQ Rub from this site and marinated my shrimp for a few hours before wrapping in bacon and skewering them....then grilled instead of broiled. Thanks!

Wow! So easy and so delicious! I purchased the 13 - 15 per pound frozen shrimp with tails on. Pro tip: it's the shells that give shrimp their taste! I cut each piece of bacon in 1/2. Wrapped the bacon around the seasoned shrimp, and then glazed them with Kinders BBQ sauce. So delicious! What a great recipe!
good one no changes
Liked this very much, if I had a family I'm sure they would have loved this.

I bought 1/2 lb of Gulf Shrimp, which are the best shrimp, which gave us 10 very large shrimp. Wrapped each in 1/2 piece of bacon. Sprinkled a lil Tony’s on them, let them sit 15 min. Then put in a preheated oven @ 450 for 11 minutes. They were so tender and tasty! Thank you for sharing this recipe that I can add to my monthly menu!

I put some B.B sauce on shrimp before cooking. Was very delicious! My 15 year old son likes to cook and he loved it too. He made a nice arrangement on a plate. I'd add it but he already ate it! Can't think of good sides for this? Any ideas?

great. made it with turkey bacon, the only change that i made. the bacon i used was thick, so i precooked until the edges were shrinking. delicious. i made them earlier in the day and then just had to pop them in the oven for 10 minutes. since i used turkey bacon, and there wasn't much fat, i just cooked them on foil without the rack.

Soooo good! My wife, who loves shrimp, asked why she had never had this dish before. She wants more! We used bbq sauce and it worked out just fine. Pre-cooked the bacon a bit and the only problem with that was we all got hungry from the smell long before it was ready. Cooking it again
Very good will be making again
I made these, & they are delicious! I will make these again!
